However, the vegetable choices felt limited, and there was too much rice in proportion to other ingredients. The Maui roll didn't meet the same standard as the 96th street location. Despite these issues, I would still go back for the sushi bowls. The service may be slower, but it's worth it as a healthier alternative to fast food. And don't forget to try the yummy bubble tea, like the strawberry flavor!

input: I stayed at this hotel for three nights on business and had a pleasant experience. Despite being close to the airport, there was minimal noise disturbance. The standard TownePlace Suite rooms were well-equipped with essential amenities. The location of the hotel is quiet, surrounded by other hotels and office buildings. It's conveniently located about a 20-minute drive from downtown and the university area, and only 5-10 minutes away from Pima Air Museum. While there aren't many restaurants nearby, there are fast food options and a delightful sandwich place called Baggins within walking distance. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful. Breakfast included standard continental options with a few hot dishes, and they also hosted a reception on weekday evenings. My only complaint is that the food and drink at the reception go quickly, so arriving early is recommended if you plan to have it as dinner. Although the area had food, there were very few soft drinks left (no diet) when I arrived 45 minutes after it started. It would be beneficial if they continuously restocked the area. However, overall, the rooms were nice, beds were comfortable, and the area felt safe.

Sectionals are expensive for unfamiliar brands, and staff prioritizes chatting over customer service. The dining sets are average and overpriced, available elsewhere for less. Overall, it's better to shop around or wait for a holiday sale for better deals on low to mediocre quality furniture.

input: My sister-in-law and I visited this restaurant on 8/28/15 and it was a disappointing experience. Despite requesting multiple times, the hostess spoke too quietly for us to hear over the background music. We were seated in a booth with a never-ending Larry King vitamin commercial on the TV, which was not enjoyable. Our waitress introduced herself and a trainee, but they were absent for the rest of the meal and we were unsure who was responsible for our table. The food took a long time to arrive, considering the restaurant was not busy. The blue cheese burger had an overwhelming amount of blue cheese and could have been better with less. The fries and onion sticks were tasty though. No one came to check if we were satisfied or needed anything and it took two requests and waiting time to get a carry-out box. Additionally, another family had been waiting for their food since before we arrived, which was concerning. Overall, I do not plan on returning to this restaurant in the future.

input: I had a wonderful lunch experience at this wine lounge with my fiancee and friend. The small table by the window provided a cozy and intimate atmosphere. The wine selection was impressive and varied, with great options to choose from. We enjoyed a bubbly and Italian orange soda. The "snacks" of lamb sausage, potato chips, and crab stuffed peppers were delicious. I particularly loved the mozzarella with prosciutto bacon bits sandwich, which was both flavorful and light. The service was prompt and polite. The rustic ambiance had a low to medium noise level. The only minor issue was the confusing bathroom door lock and handle. Overall, I would highly recommend this place for lunch.

input: I recently tried out this Thai restaurant and I would give it 4-5 stars. It was my first visit and I found the food to be delicious. The shrimp spring rolls were especially fresh and the peanut sauce was tasty. The tom yum soup was a bit too spicy for my liking, but still had a good sour flavor. The pad thai and drunken noodle dishes were also enjoyable, although the noodles in the pad thai were a bit overdone. The portions were slightly smaller than other places in the area. The owner was friendly and attentive, even coming outside to talk with me about the food. The restaurant has a cute setup in a quaint house, but it may not be ideal if it's crowded. Overall, I think it's worth a try for Thai food fans. I used a Living Social deal, which made the total bill for two people, including an appetizer, soup, and a drink, to be around $24.

input: My husband and I reserved a Corolla-sized car online, but requested an upgrade to a Camry at Avis Rent A Car in Reno. After some discussion, we received the Camry we wanted. The staff was professional, but the rental price of $800 for five days seemed high. We had already purchased insurance for $150. The car itself was great during our vacation. However, upon dropping off the car, we found out that a weekly rate would have been just $15 more. The upgrade had cost us an extra $20 per day. I will not rent from Avis again, opting for Hertz or Dollar and making phone reservations instead. In hindsight, the extra insurance was unnecessary as my personal insurance covers everything.

The bacon is thick and tasty, albeit slightly overcooked. With reasonable prices and excellent service, this is the perfect spot for a satisfying homemade breakfast.

input: Sweet Confections on Magazine St had a beautifully sweet ending to our trip to NOLA. After a delicious lunch at Cochon, we stumbled upon this charming spot. We tried a chocolate cupcake with mocha filling and truffles in raspberry, creme brulee, and orange flavors. The cupcake was good, but the mocha filling stole the show. The raspberry truffle was my favorite, with its perfect balance of dark chocolate. The coffee was a delightful chaser, not too overpowering, and I didn't even need milk or sugar. The seating was nice, with enough room for our group of six. The service was great, with helpful staff suggesting flavors and labeling. I give it 4 out of 5 stars, as having one more staff member would benefit the overall service.

input: Unfortunately, Millers did not live up to expectations. The guacamole portion was huge but lacked flavor, while the zinger boneless wings were enjoyable, along with the attractive hostesses. The server was pleasant and attentive, addressing issues promptly. However, the wilted side salad was disappointing and the main dishes lacked flavor and presentation. The plastic dishes and high price for a lackluster experience were discouraging. The desire for dessert was overshadowed by the risk of disappointment. Overall, the experience did not meet expectations, and the reviewer does not plan to return for dining in, although the husband might order wings for takeout.

input:
I heard about this place from a fellow Yelp Elite and decided to give it a try with my SO. We went on a Saturday morning and had to wait in line. 

The takoyaki appetizer was delicious - perfectly cooked and topped with sauces. The fried octopus was good but didn't come with enough mayo. 

Unfortunately, the ramen noodles were overcooked and didn't fit well with the dishes. The broth was flavorful, but the red chili one was too spicy and covered up the depth. I preferred the black garlic broth. 

Overall, the food was tasty and reasonably priced. The decor was nice, but there were screaming kids running around which made our meal unpleasant.

The lack of shades at the front window can make it uncomfortable. The food was okay, but my pulled pork wrap had a lot of gristle. The cornbread pancakes were tasty though. The payment process is inconvenient as you pay afterwards. I regret bringing my brother here for brunch, it's a dive. Don't expect traditional breakfast service or a nice atmosphere. It's cheap, but you get what you pay for.

input: I recently enjoyed an express lunch at this charming restaurant with old school decor featuring dark woods and a copper tile ceiling. The deal included a choice of soup with the entree of the day, and I must say, the gumbo and crab bisque were fantastic. The gumbo had a rich flavor with a touch of heat from the andouille sausage, while the crab bisque was perfectly seasoned with old bay style seasoning and had just the right amount of shredded crab. The entree, garganelli with roast pork ragu, mushrooms, and creole tomatoes, was a delightful blend of flavors with a light sauce that highlighted the dish. The roast pork itself was tender, caramelized, and left me craving more. Overall, a satisfying lunch experience in a visually appealing setting.

input: Overall, this restaurant is small but conveniently located on the wharf. Despite the limited seating, the wait time was short. Sitting at the bar was a good option. The noise level was a bit high due to the small space. The service provided was excellent. The crab sandwich was disappointing, served on plain white bread. However, the fried shrimp was enjoyable - not greasy or heavy, with moist and flavorful shrimp. It is worth noting that the menu only offers shellfish options. As a non-seafood enthusiast, I was pleasantly surprised by the shrimp and onion rings. However, my seafood enthusiast husband did not enjoy the crab sandwich. If you love shellfish and appreciate the great location, this place could be worth a try.

input: Three of us flew in from Chicago and decided to stop by this place for a quick bite. We arrived close to 3 and asked if we could wait until happy hour to order. Despite being empty, the place was nicely decorated and had a spacious feel. We all tried their cocktails, with the Mint Julep falling short but the gin drink exceeding expectations. Our order also included Mac and cheese, fries, Brussels sprouts, and a pretzel. I skipped the sprouts, but everything else was delicious! The prices during happy hour were a steal. Rest assured, I'll be back on my next trip to Reno!

input: Finding a vegetarian restaurant in New Orleans was initially challenging, as many places were unwilling to accommodate our needs. However, in recent years, more restaurants are recognizing this and offering vegetarian options. Muriel's Jackson Square had a vegetarian menu, and we made reservations to ensure we would be able to eat. The cocktails were delicious, and we enjoyed the veggie crepe, despite the seafood sauce. The main course was a variety of veggie dishes, some of which were tasty, but some could have been cooked longer. Overall, we left with satisfied stomachs and had a pleasant vegetarian night out.

Don't forget to try their great selection of wines and craft beers.

input: This place offers the best roast chicken I've ever tried. The chicken itself is moist and crispy with a nice smoky flavor. The aroma is hypnotizing and makes your mouth water. The double chicken family meal is perfect for a family of four, with ample portions of chicken, fries, and cole slaw. The dipping sauces, particularly the mustard-based one with a chipotle flair, are delicious. The wedge fries are filling and there are plenty to go around. The portion size was so big that we had leftovers. The service is excellent, and the owners are friendly. I would choose this place over Popeyes or KFC due to the generous portions, healthier options, and better service. I will definitely be returning because I know I'll be craving their delicious chicken.

input: This is a typical Broad Ripple charming spot with a small, trendy, and bustling atmosphere. Unfortunately, they do not take reservations, which can be annoying for those traveling from another part of town. However, the cocktails were creative and delicious, and the server's suggestions were on point. The guacamole was tasty, but came with nuts despite requesting them to be left off. The Harvest salad was a highlight with its delightful combination of fruit and root vegetables. The Veracruz Trigger fish and Serrano Scallops were both delicious, accompanied by interesting white sweet mashed potatoes. The Tostones were a bit dry, but dipped in the Stewed Black Beans, they tasted great. Unfortunately, there were no gluten-free, dairy-free dessert options available. Overall, it's worth a visit, just make sure to arrive before 7 pm on a Friday to secure a table.

input: I've been to Jackson's multiple times and finally decided to leave a review. The panini Reuben was delicious with great use of garlic and perfectly sliced meat. However, the salad came out at the same time as the sandwich, which was not ideal, and the presentation was a bit sloppy. The sandwich was served directly on a plate instead of a napkin, causing the bread to get soggy if it sits for too long. The price is a bit high, but the food and drink quality justifies it. They have a great selection of wines and beers to choose from. The wait staff is generally friendly but can sometimes be short or distracted. The wait time for drinks can vary, with my longest wait being 15 minutes during a lunch rush. Overall, it was a good experience and I will return.

input: I was excited to try Lee How Fook after reading positive Yelp reviews, but unfortunately, I was left disappointed. The small size of the restaurant didn't bother me, but it's advisable to make reservations due to limited tables. The service was adequate, although understanding the server was a bit difficult. As for the food, the appetizers were delicious with a flavorful dipping sauce. However, the sweet & sour chicken was overly sweet and the vegetables were undercooked. The pan-fried noodle dishes lacked flavor and the supposed spicy beef wasn't spicy at all. Overall, I left full but unsatisfied.

input: My girlfriends and I dined at the Creole House for dinner due to its proximity to our hotel. The bacon garlic oysters were average, as the flavors were overpowered by the cheese and bacon. The jumbo buffalo wings were tasty and well-seasoned. The jumbalaya pasta lacked flavor and was our least favorite, while the blackened red fish was just okay. The sautéed veggies accompanying the dish were excessively salty. The canal street red fish wasn't great and lacked garlic sauce. The paddle boat drinks tasted good but were more juice than alcohol. Overall, the food was underwhelming, earning the restaurant a solid 3 stars. On a positive note, our server, Alexander, provided excellent hospitality and tried his best to ensure our satisfaction.

input: This is hands down my favorite sushi spot in Delaware. The menu is simple yet executed perfectly, with reasonably priced rolls that are bursting with fish. The use of flash-frozen sashimi grade fish doesn't compromise the flavor, as the color, texture, taste, and smell are all flawless. The spicy tuna roll is nothing short of incredible, thanks to the combination of kewpie mayo, sriracha, and sichimi powder. I can't get enough of this place, often having it for lunch every day for weeks. The addition of short-grain brown sushi rice has been a fantastic touch. Watching YC Park, The Sushiman, work his magic is mesmerizing, as he effortlessly skins a cucumber with a sushi knife and transforms it into a nori sheet for his rolls. The temaki rolls are massive, packed with fish, and the nigiri is beautifully presented. While I save my 5-star rating for places that serve locally caught fresh fish, Tokyo is a must-visit for sushi lovers. Support the owners in these challenging times and skip Kooma and save Mikimotos for a special night out. If you crave sushi, look no further than Tokyo!

input: Prohibition is a nice, old school space with a long bar that feels reminiscent of western establishments, which is a bit unusual for Philadelphia. The atmosphere is not too loud, making conversations easy, especially during early hours. The service from the bar staff is great. They offer several beers on tap, including a solid local IPA, but the wine selection is limited. Despite having a small menu, the food is very good, with standout dishes like the elote and cucumber salad. However, the star of the menu is the brat plate, served on a cool wooden board and accompanied by German potato salad, sauerkraut, pretzel, and a delicious hot salsa/relish. It's worth noting that Prohibition is located in a somewhat questionable neighborhood, which may deter some visitors from walking back if it's late at night.

input: Fresh Market has helpful staff, specifically Thomas in the meat section. However, the overall experience went downhill from there. The Swiss cheese we ordered was poorly cut, resulting in one clump instead of slices. The ricotta cheese we bought was bad despite being within the expiration date. The tomatoes on the vine spoiled quickly, and prices were high while selection was poor. The pound cakes were dry and tasteless. Although the store was clean with parking available, it was ultimately a disappointing shopping trip. Additionally, conflicting information regarding cash withdrawal limits added to the dissatisfaction. It is recommended to shop at Weaver's Way, Whole Foods, or Wegmann's instead.

input: We had an excellent experience at this restaurant! The food was delicious and the service was top-notch. Despite a long wait on the formal side, we opted for the bar area and were pleasantly surprised that the full menu was available. The firecracker shrimp arrived quickly, and we enjoyed live music from a great band. The attentive servers made our visit even better. We ordered a variety of items, including alcohol, appetizers, entrees, salad, and dessert. Both the salmon and swordfish were fantastic. We also loved the huge fish tank, which we recognized from the famous TV show "Tanked". Overall, this restaurant offers not only good food and a nice view but also a memorable dining experience. We will definitely be coming back.

Absolutely delicious! I wish I could have this everyday. Five stars!
